_loader_notes: Image manifest (AGENTS.md R11 and X1). One entry per image slug used anywhere in /content or the app. The images table and Supabase storage follow this file: upload a file, then fill file, photographer, source_url, licence_source and model_release, and set status to 'ready'.
same_as means reuse that slug's file instead of sourcing a new one.
Show a tidy placeholder (brand-tinted shape with the relevant icon) for any slug that isn't ready.

style_guide.summary: Real women training in real, warm, well-lit gyms. Half the people photos are connection shots (smiling, often towards the camera, relaxed between sets); half are in-action shots (focused, mid-exercise, eyes on the movement). Authentic and candid, never posed glamour.
people: Women only in frame (another woman's hand or arm is fine, like reference 1). No men.
Aged roughly 18 to 45, diverse ethnicities, skin tones, body sizes and builds across the set. Aim for no more than about a third of the set to look alike.
Natural, confident expressions: genuine smiles or calm focus. Never strained, pained or exhausted.
Real gym clothes in varied, muted colours. Sports bras and crop tops are fine, but the photo is framed on her face, hands and the movement.
framing: Never crop or angle to make the stomach, chest or bum the focal point. If a shot reads as a body shot, reject it.
Eye level or slightly below, 35 to 85 mm look, shallow depth of field so the gym blurs behind her.
Equipment must be real and recognisable (dumbbell racks, benches, cables, plate-loaded machines, racks).
Leave clear space for text on heroes and covers: subject off-centre, background calm on one side.
Check every image in its crops: card 4:3, hero 16:9 or 4:5, tile 1:1.
light_and_colour: Warm, natural light: window light or warm practical lights, mid to bright exposure.
Dark gym backgrounds are fine only if she's well lit and the photo feels warm (references 4 and 6). No black and white, no gritty or very low-key shots (reference 2's grading is out).
One consistent grade across the app: warm white balance, gently lifted shadows, natural skin tones, no heavy filters or neon tints.
never: Visible brand logos, gym names or watermarks (e.g. Gold's Gym logos on dumbbells in reference 6). Retouch them out or pick another photo.
Text, captions or stock-site UI in the image.
Mirror selfies, phones showing screens, before and after or progress-style body photos.
AI-generated people or AI-generated exercise demonstrations.
The same photo twice on one screen, and ideally anywhere in the app (the only reuse allowed is where same_as says so).
style_guide.equipment_photos: Machine guide and onboarding equipment photos show the machine on its own, three-quarter angle, whole machine in frame, bright clean gym, nobody using it.
style_guide.food_photos: Bright natural light, real kitchens and tables, 45 degrees or overhead, the exact dish in the recipe with no ingredients that aren't in it. Hands are fine; no faces.
licensing: Every file needs licence_source, photographer and source_url filled in.

Pexels and Unsplash licences allow commercial use but don't include model releases. For people photos used in marketing (App Store screenshots, paywall, onboarding, ads), prefer photos with model releases from a paid library (e.g. Adobe Stock or iStock), and record model_release.
Never use photos from Pinterest, Google Images or social media, even as placeholders in builds you share.
style_guide.references: Sacha's references (keep in design/photo-references/): 1 fist bump smiling at camera, 3 lat pulldown, 4 curl, 5 stability ball plank pair, 6 sitting on gym floor laughing. Reference 2 (black and white squat) is NOT the direction.

Pose differs from the brief (standing, not seated against a wall, no towel visible), but it is the right kind of connection moment for a people hero.

The expression is calm focus, closer to an in-action shot than a warm connection shot.
